text.p: LIFFE sugar futures edged up on Monday to end firmer in what traders said was good volume considering that many were absent ahead of the New Year holiday.
By the close, 1012 lots had been traded. Front month March last traded at the high, up $2.80 at $310.00.
The market was following New York up, traders said. The rise was no more than a continuation of Friday's trend.

On the fundamentals front, Pakistan's sugar production for 1996/97 (July/June) fell 42.87 percent to 388,272 tonnes by December 15 compared to 679,635 tonnes in the year-ago period, Pakistan Sugar Mills Association said on Monday. --London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
